Before running, this seat read the script's leaf printer and identified the one path by which a VALUE reaches the output -- `shown = s if (CLOSED.fullmatch(s) and not hit)`, where CLOSED is [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,63} -- so a bare upper-case alphanumeric token (base32-shaped) under an innocuously-named key would print verbatim, since KEYBAD tests the KEY and COOKIE and JWT need their own shapes. So the residual is named, not hidden, and the order puts the final read on this seat -- which is where it belongs. every_verbatim_printed_leaf_was_inspecte.description: THE CONTROL THAT MATTERED MOST ON THIS ORDER, because anything the script prints is committed to git and the subject is a sign-in receipt. The script hashes a leaf's value unless it fully matches an upper-case closed-token pattern and trips none of four checks; that whitelist is the single path by which receipt text can reach the repo, and the issuer declares it. So every leaf that printed verbatim was enumerated and read, rather than the count being trusted.
every_verbatim_printed_leaf_was_inspecte.expected_landed: every verbatim-printed leaf is a short closed enum; none is long, none carries lower case or punctuation, none is high-entropy
every_verbatim_printed_leaf_was_inspecte.expected_not_landed: any verbatim value that could be a credential -- a base32-shaped token, a long opaque string, anything not an enum -- which on a real receipt is a secret committed to git
every_verbatim_printed_leaf_was_inspecte.observed: 120 LEAF rows: 61 strings shown as length+hash, 43 bool/null/number/list rows, and 16 printed verbatim. The 16 reduce to THREE distinct values: NOT_LIVE (14, the probe_state and probe_reason of steps 1 to 7), AUTH_FAILED (failure_class) and NO_AUTHENTICATED_PROBE (reason). Longest is 22 characters; 0 of the 16 fail the test ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$. All three are the diagnosis st32 was built to record. NOTHING secret-shaped printed, and the enumeration is on the record so a reader can re-check it rather than take this seat's word.

the_FOUND_verdict_was_decomposed_rather_.description: The order says a FOUND verdict is a finding to report as the four counts. Reported as the bare number 33 it reads as 'the receipt holds 33 secrets', which is false in a way that would have shaped the CTO's condition-2 judgment. The counter's own definition is what separates the readings.
the_FOUND_verdict_was_decomposed_rather_.expected_landed: the 33 attributed to KEY-NAME matches rather than value matches, the three value-shaped counters read, and the 33 broken out by field name (which the order permits)
the_FOUND_verdict_was_decomposed_rather_.expected_not_landed: relaying 33 and FOUND without saying what was matched, or quoting any value to make the point
the_FOUND_verdict_was_decomposed_rather_.observed: posted_value_key=33 increments on KEYBAD.search against the leaf NAME. The three counters that test the VALUE each read 0: cookie_like=0 (name=long-opaque-value), tokenised_url=0 (a URL with a query or fragment), jwt_like=0 (eyJ...). The 33 decompose by name as 25 credential-named fields -- login_submission.password_field, cookie_names[0..9] on both probe arms, session_cookie_names_present[0..1] on both -- and 8 whose names are the probe pair's own arms. All 33 print as length+hash (33 of 33 verified), so the decomposition cost no value.
